body: An aircraft moving through a surrounding gas can generate aerodynamic forces. A wing redirects air and experiences lift. Weight acts toward Earth. Drag opposes motion through the air, and many aircraft use propulsion to supply thrust.

A spacecraft with its own propellant can accelerate by expelling it, even in near-vacuum. Rockets carry launch vehicles beyond dense air. Once in orbit, a spacecraft can continue to fall around a larger body while its instruments observe Earth or distant objects. Some spacecraft carry people and many operate without a crew.

limitations: The Wright Flyer, Saturn V launch and a modern booster recovery illustrate particular machines, objectives and conditions.
purpose: Introduce forces and energy underlying atmospheric flight and spacecraft motion.
